newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Price correction hits Zimbabwe stocks. [CORRECTED 17:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Price correction hits Zimbabwe stocks. [CORRECTED 17:55 GMT]

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks reversed their upward march on Wednesday, hit by a price-correction which brokers said should be temporary as investor sentiment was still high on expectations of lending rate cuts following a dramatic fall in annual inflation.
The key industrial index, which has soared 80.7 percent over the past nine months, dropped 39.26 points to close at 7,137.29 after a day of mixed and active trade.

"We were expecting some profit-taking but the question was when. So today was a departure from the trend but the market will pick up again. This should be a mere correction with prices having risen so much as to induce people to sell," one broker said.
Among the winners on Wednesday, finance house Finhold surged 100 cents to 900, food group Natfoods and pottery-maker Ariston each rose 50 cents to 650 and 1,350 respectively.
Soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes gained 35 cents to 660 while multi-industrial group Tedco at 470, sugar producer Hippo at 860 and pharmaceutical firm Caps at 250 all put on 10 cents.

Bankers Barclays and blue-chip conglomerate Delta traded at overnight levels in reasonable turnover and in line with the day's trend (corrects from "but against the trend"), merchant bankers FMB slid 100 cents to 3,400, multi-industrial group Mash and pork processor Colcom each dropped 25 cents to 125 and 340 respectively.

Finance group UDC shed 20 cents to 220, as did discount house DCZ to 130, food-canning firm Cairns lost 15 cents to 800 while hotel chain Zimsun at 425 and packaging group Hunyani at 390 were both 10 cents lower.

Minings were also active although weaker with gold producer Ashanti sliding 500 cents to 15,500, Rio Tinto dropping 200 cents to 3,300, Falgold down 20 cents to 180 and Wankie Colliery slipping five cents off to 350. Falcon was the only winner, rising 50 cents to 1,800.
The mining index ended 42.35 points down at 1,373.97.
